docs.title: Production Optimization
docs.text: Field-wide production optimization and well allocation using ML.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This machine learning system is part of the Oil & Gas ML Portfolio by Kelvin J Cabrera.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Synthetic Data Generator -> Scikit-Learn Training -> Flask API -> Streamlit Dashboard

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Data Generation: Domain-aware synthetic data with physical correlations
  • Model Training: Scikit-learn pipelines (Random Forest, Isolation Forest) with MLflow tracking
  • API: Flask/FastAPI with API key authentication
  • Dashboard: Streamlit interactive web interface
  • Testing: pytest with model evaluation metrics (R2, accuracy, F1)

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
pip install -r requirements.txt
python train.py
python app.py
streamlit run streamlit_app.py

docs.title: API Endpoints
docs.text:
Method Endpoint Description GET / Service info and available models POST /predict/{model} Run inference (requires API key)

Authentication

All API endpoints require an X-API-Key header. Set API_KEY in your environment.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
All API requests require an API key sent via the X-API-Key header.

import requests

headers = {"X-API-Key": "your-api-key"}
response = requests.post("http://localhost:5000/predict/model", json={...}, headers=headers)

docs.title: GET /
docs.text:
Returns service information and available models.

Response:

{"service": "Production Optimization", "models": ["model1", "model2"]}

docs.title: POST /predict/{model_name}
docs.text:
Run inference on a trained model.

Request Body:

{"features": {"feature_1": 0.5, "feature_2": 1.2}}

Response:

{"prediction": 0.85, "model": "model_name"}

docs.title: Error Codes
docs.text: Code Description 401 Invalid or missing API key 404 Model not found 422 Invalid input format

docs.title: Data Layer
docs.text:
• Source: Synthetic data generator (generate_field_data)
  • Samples: 2,000 field operation records
  • Features: 8 parameters (7 numeric + 1 categorical)
  • Targets: net_profit (regression), production_efficiency (regression)

docs.title: Field Optimizer
docs.text:
• Algorithm: GradientBoostingRegressor
  • Task: Predict net profit (USD) for field operations
  • Input: 8 features (7 numeric + 1 categorical encoded)
  • Output: Net profit (continuous)
  • Serialization: joblib (.joblib)
  • Cross-validation: CV R2 score reported

docs.title: Allocation Model
docs.text:
• Algorithm: RandomForestRegressor
  • Task: Predict production efficiency (0-1 scale)
  • Input: Same 8 features
  • Output: Production efficiency (continuous)
  • Serialization: joblib (.joblib)
  • Cross-validation: CV R2 score reported

docs.title: Preprocessing Pipeline
docs.text:
• ColumnTransformer with:
  • StandardScaler for 7 numeric features
  • OneHotEncoder for lift_type (4 categories)
  • Separate preprocessors for each model target
  • Saved as preprocessor_opt.joblib and preprocessor_alloc.joblib

docs.title: API Layer
docs.text:
• Framework: Flask
  • Port: 5014
  • Format: JSON request/response
  • Endpoints: 5 (optimize, allocate, health, models, docs)

docs.title: Dashboard Layer
docs.text:
• Frontend: HTML/CSS/JS (Jinja2 templates)
  • Charts: Plotly.js for feature importance visualization
  • Theme: Dark theme UI

docs.title: Net Profit Optimization Flow
docs.text:
1. User provides field parameters
  2. Input wrapped in DataFrame
  3. Preprocessor transforms features (scale + encode)
  4. GradientBoostingRegressor predicts net profit
  5. Response returns prediction + input echo

docs.title: Production Efficiency Flow
docs.text:
1. User provides same field parameters
  2. Separate preprocessor transforms features
  3. RandomForestRegressor predicts efficiency
  4. Response returns prediction + input echo

docs.title: Feature Processing
docs.text: Feature Type Transform Description well_count numeric StandardScaler Number of wells total_water_rate numeric StandardScaler Water production rate total_gas_rate numeric StandardScaler Gas production rate water_injection_rate numeric StandardScaler Injection rate operating_cost_usd numeric StandardScaler Operating expenses revenue_per_bbl numeric StandardScaler Oil revenue per barrel artificial_lift_power_kw numeric StandardScaler Lift power consumption lift_type categorical OneHotEncoder ESP/rod_pump/gas_lift/progressive_cavity

docs.title: Dockerfile
docs.text:
FROM python:3.9-slim

WORKDIR /app

COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

COPY . .

RUN python train.py

EXPOSE 5014

CMD ["python", "app.py"]

docs.title: Build and Run
docs.text:
docker build -t production-optimization .
docker run -p 5014:5014 production-optimization

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
version: '3.8'
services:
  production-optimization:
    build: .
    ports:
      - "5014:5014"
    environment:
      - FLASK_ENV=production
    volumes:
      - model-data:/app/outputs

volumes:
  model-data:

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Description Default FLASK_ENV Flask environment mode development PORT Server port 5014

docs.title: Production Considerations
docs.text:
• Use gunicorn for production serving: bash gunicorn -w 4 -b 0.0.0.0:5014 app:app
  • Set debug=False in app.py (already set)
  • Configure reverse proxy (nginx) for SSL termination
  • Set up health check monitoring on /api/health
  • Use a process manager (systemd, supervisor) for auto-restart
  • Models serialized with joblib for efficient loading

docs.title: Training Pipeline
docs.text:
1. python train.py generates synthetic field data
  2. Separate preprocessors fitted for each target
  3. Models trained with cross-validation
  4. Artifacts saved to outputs/models/:
  5. field_optimizer.joblib - Net profit predictor
  6. allocation_model.joblib - Efficiency predictor
  7. preprocessor_opt.joblib - Profit preprocessor
  8. preprocessor_alloc.joblib - Efficiency preprocessor
  9. training_results.json - CV scores summary

docs.title: CI/CD
docs.text:
GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml): - Runs on push to main - Installs dependencies - Runs training pipeline - Executes API tests (pytest)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Production Optimization system uses machine learning to predict net profit and production efficiency for oil field operations, helping optimize well allocation and resource management.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.8+
  • pip

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
cd production-optimization
pip install -r requirements.txt

docs.title: Train Models
docs.text:
python train.py

This generates 2,000 synthetic field operation records and trains: - Field Optimizer (GradientBoostingRegressor) - Predicts net profit - Allocation Model (RandomForestRegressor) - Predicts production efficiency

docs.title: Run the Server
docs.text:
python app.py

Open http://localhost:5014 in your browser.

docs.title: Typical Workflow
docs.text:
1. Enter field parameters (well count, rates, costs, lift type)
  2. Call /api/optimize to predict net profit
  3. Call /api/allocate to predict production efficiency
  4. Compare scenarios by varying lift_type, costs, or revenue
  5. Use feature importances to identify optimization targets

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Models not loaded: Run python train.py first
  • Missing fields: All 8 fields are required
  • Invalid lift_type: Must be one of ESP, rod_pump, gas_lift, progressive_cavity
  • Port in use: Change port in app.py

Elaborado por Ing. Kelvin Cabrera

docs.title: Training Pipeline
docs.text:
The training pipeline follows these steps:

  1. Data Generation: data_generator.py creates synthetic data with domain-specific physical correlations
  2. Preprocessing: Feature scaling via StandardScaler
  3. Training: Random Forest or Isolation Forest via scikit-learn
  4. Evaluation: R2 score, accuracy, classification report
  5. Logging: MLflow tracks parameters, metrics, and artifacts
  6. Serialization: Model + scaler + metadata saved as .pkl via joblib

docs.title: Model Files
docs.text:
Models are stored in outputs/models/*.pkl as dictionaries with:

Key Description model Trained scikit-learn estimator scaler Fitted StandardScaler feature_names List of input feature names target_name Target variable name metrics Evaluation metrics from training

docs.title: Retraining
docs.text:
To retrain:

python train.py

This will update the model files in outputs/models/ and log results to MLflow.
